clue.text: Odds against racehorse, Royal Gem

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered on a horse at the off
Arkle was a celebrated Irish steeplechaser of the 1960s
R is the usual abbreviation for royal, as in RN

explanation.surface: A punter backs a horse called Royal Gem against the odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Gem' reads as the horse's name; it splits into R and the definition. SP (starting price) is how British bookmakers quote odds; Arkle was a famous racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparkler is informal slang for a diamond or other glittering precious stone.

clue.text: Driver for member of upper house pockets pounds

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: pockets means holds inside, as a pocket holds coins

parts.note: a peer sits in the House of Lords
L stands for pound, so LL is pounds

explanation.surface: A driver working for a member of the House of Lords pockets cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' looks like a chauffeur for a lord, but it means the thing that drives a ship or aircraft.
explanation.definitionFit: A propeller is the rotating blade that drives a ship or aircraft forward.

clue.text: Austere conditions set up for us

parts.note: to rig is to set up equipment
ours means belonging to us

explanation.surface: Hardships arranged for our benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigours are hardships or harsh conditions, which an austere life brings.

clue.text: Standard that may be raised to no effect

indicators.text: that may be raised to no effect
indicators.note: in a down clue raising a word reads it upwards, and here that changes nothing

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A standard that can be lifted without making any difference.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raised' means read upwards; 'to no effect' says the word is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: A level is a standard of attainment, as in a high level of skill.

clue.text: Legendary thing king pulled from stone at last

indicators.note: pulled from means taken out of the word for stone

parts.note: a rock is a stone
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A legend in which a king at last pulls a sword from the stone.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface evokes Arthur drawing the sword from the stone. 'at last' tells you the K comes from the end of ROCK.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant mythical bird of Arabian legend.

clue.text: Lighting-up time, one rule I'd reverse

indicators.note: the instruction at the end turns the whole string of pieces backwards

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
a law is a rule
I'd contracts to ID

explanation.surface: Someone announces a lighting-up time and a rule they would like to overturn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns ILAWID round into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindu festival of lights is celebrated by lighting lamps, so it is a lighting-up time.

clue.text: Needs five changes to description of moat's function

indicators.note: changes means the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone needs five alterations to an account of what a moat is for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges NEEDS FIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: A moat protects a castle, so the adjective for guarding against attack describes its job.

clue.text: Prevent fighting —— make fine beginning in force

parts.note: war is fighting
to do is to make or perform
F is the abbreviation for fine, used on pencils

indicators.note: takes the first letter of the word force

explanation.surface: Someone stops a fight by forcefully imposing a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning in' gives F from force.
explanation.definitionFit: To ward off something is to fend it off or prevent it.

clue.text: Body of water, not the first in marsh

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word for marsh is dropped

parts.note: a slough is a bog or marsh

explanation.surface: A stretch of water that is not the main one in a marsh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not the first in' drops S from SLOUGH.
explanation.definitionFit: A lough is an Irish lake or sea inlet, a body of water.

clue.text: Carve name into piece of wood — pine

indicators.note: carving a letter into the log places it inside the word

parts.note: a log is a piece of wood

explanation.surface: A woodcarver cuts a name into a piece of pine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pine' looks like the type of wood, but it is the verb meaning yearn; 'Carve' just sets up the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To pine for something is to long for it, a synonym meaning yearn.

clue.text: Very ferocious, awfully loud

indicators.note: awfully suggests something badly done, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone or something is very fierce and terribly loud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' rearranges V plus FEROCIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Vociferous describes someone shouting noisily, a synonym for loud.

clue.text: People generally in near-anarchy in foreign party

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other
anarchy is disorder, so the letters of the word near are thrown into disorder

parts.note: the public is people in general

explanation.surface: Ordinary people living in near-anarchy within some foreign political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'near-anarchy' looks like one idea, but 'anarchy' scrambles NEAR into RE...AN, which surrounds PUBLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: The Republicans are one of the two main US political parties, foreign from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: Conveyance to move with the waves, going to Lewis

parts.note: a car is a conveyance
a ship rolls as the waves move it

explanation.surface: A vehicle rocking on the waves as it heads to the Isle of Lewis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lewis' looks like the Scottish island but is the first name of the author of Alice in Wonderland.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the pen name of the writer of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Pacific island in centre of storm bears the brunt

indicators.note: takes the middle letter of each of the next four words

explanation.surface: A Pacific island in the middle of a storm takes the worst of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'centre of' takes O, A, H and U from storm, bears, the, brunt.
explanation.definitionFit: Oahu is the Hawaiian island where Honolulu stands, in the Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: A funeral song for Scotsman?

parts.note: a funeral is a person's last rites, so funeral suggests last
an air is a song or tune

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a funeral song for a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition by example: this is a common Scottish first name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alastair is a typically Scottish given name, so a Scotsman might bear it.

clue.text: Relieve patriarch in a recent case

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: late can mean recent, as in the late news
Levi was one of the sons of Jacob, a patriarch of Israel

explanation.surface: Someone helps an old patriarch in a recent legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case' is surface dressing; the patriarch Levi, son of Jacob, is placed after the first two letters of A LATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain is to relieve or ease it.

clue.text: Popular little woman arrested following bad report

indicators.note: arrested means held, so one piece is caught inside the other

parts.note: in means popular, fashionable
Amy is one of the March sisters in Little Women

explanation.surface: A well-liked young woman is arrested after a damaging report.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy March is the youngest of the sisters in Louisa May Alcott's novel Little Women, hence 'little woman'.
explanation.definitionFit: Infamy is notoriety, an evil reputation or bad report about someone.

clue.text: Beneath old city in midlands kingdom, lake rapidly changing

indicators.note: in a down clue the lake piece is placed below the rest
the old city goes inside the kingdom

parts.note: Mercia was the Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands
Ur was an ancient Sumerian city

explanation.surface: Below an ancient city in a Midlands kingdom, a lake keeps changing.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was the Anglo-Saxon kingdom covering the English Midlands; Ur was the city of Abraham in ancient Mesopotamia.
explanation.definitionFit: Mercurial describes a temperament prone to sudden shifts of mood, like quicksilver.

clue.text: Small stones finally smaller, squashed by hammer

indicators.note: squashed by means held tightly inside the other piece

parts.note: a gavel is an auctioneer's or judge's hammer

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word smaller

explanation.surface: Small stones end up crushed even smaller under a hammer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' gives R, which 'squashed by' puts inside GAVEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Gravel is a loose mass of small stones and pebbles.

clue.text: Part of house roofed over, and also secured

indicators.note: secured means held safely inside the following words

explanation.surface: A section of a house has been given a roof and made safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secured' points to the letters held in 'over, and also'.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed open gallery along the outside of a house.

clue.text: Homely feature of room for army command

definitions.meaning: a hearth with burning logs, a cosy domestic feature
the order given to soldiers to start shooting

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both an uncovered hearth fire and the military order to start shooting.

clue.text: Mean to take part in suitable aesthetic production

indicators.note: one piece joins in by going inside the other

parts.note: fit means suitable
near means mean, stingy

explanation.surface: A stingy person joining in a suitably artistic production.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mean' looks like a verb but is the adjective stingy, NEAR in old slang.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine art is creative work such as painting or sculpture valued for beauty.

clue.text: Extra-short fight

indicators.note: short means cut off at the end, losing its last letter

parts.note: spare means extra

explanation.surface: A boxing bout that is extremely brief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extra-short' reads as one word meaning very short; it is SPARE cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to fight, especially to box in practice or argue.

clue.text: Uncomplicated scheme I entered

indicators.note: the letter I goes into the word for scheme

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

explanation.surface: A simple scheme that I joined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entered' puts I inside PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Plain means simple and straightforward, without complication.

clue.text: Huge book isn't finished, I sense

indicators.note: the word for book loses its ending

parts.note: a volume is a book
nous is common sense

explanation.surface: Someone says a huge book is not finished, and they can feel it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'isn't finished' drops the last letter of VOLUME.
explanation.definitionFit: Voluminous means bulky or of great volume, a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Small person said to have strength

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a mite is a small child or tiny creature

explanation.surface: A tiny person is reputed to be very strong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' gives a word that sounds like MITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Might means power or strength.

clue.text: Not agreeing to acquire saw

parts.note: to gain is to acquire
a saw is a proverb or saying

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to agree to buy a saw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the tool, but it is the noun meaning proverb.
explanation.definitionFit: Gainsaying means denying or contradicting, the opposite of agreeing.

clue.text: Commercial premises in name only

parts.note: the word in is used as written; that the letters also run on into name is a coincidence, since this is a charade
N is the abbreviation for name; the run of letters across in name is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A business that exists in name only.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only' just rounds off the surface; the wordplay is IN plus N.
explanation.definitionFit: An inn is a pub or hotel, a commercial establishment.

clue.text: Related to a head of state? That's not good

indicators.note: the following letter is not included, so it is taken out

parts.note: a king is a head of state

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are related to a monarch, and hears that is no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not good' removes G from A KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Akin means related by blood or similar in nature.

clue.text: Where traveller may keep clothes for emergency

definitions.meaning: as a precaution, should something happen

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally means inside luggage and idiomatically means as a precaution.

clue.text: Perhaps a short acceptance of apology

definitions.text: Perhaps a short acceptance of apology

parts.words: Perhaps a short acceptance of apology
parts.note: a brief polite reply someone might give when told sorry, brushing the apology aside

explanation.definitionFit: Said in response to an apology, the phrase means there is no need to apologise.
